h1: The 6 Best Lightweight Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six lightweight lawn mowers from reel to cordless, sorted by cutting width, power source and the yard each one suits.
summary: The EGO POWER+ 21-Inch is our best overall because it gives full-width coverage on a cordless platform. The Greenworks 40V 16-Inch is the balanced pick for small to mid-size lawns, and the Litheli 14-Inch is the budget cordless winner. The American Lawn Mower reel is the lightest option here, with no battery or cord at all.
intro: Most people shopping for a light mower make one mistake: they compare the weight on the box and ignore the power source. A corded mower drags a cable behind you, a battery mower carries its cell on board, and a reel mower carries nothing but the blades. The right answer depends on how much grass you have and where the outlet is.

We reviewed six mowers on paper, covering a manual reel, corded electrics and cordless models from 14 to 21 inches. We ranked them on cutting width versus manageability, power-source convenience, adjustability and the type of lawn each suits, using the spec sheets and owner feedback rather than lab claims.

products.name: EGO POWER+ 21-Inch Cordless Electric Lawn Mower with Battery and Charger (LM2114)
products.verdict: A full 21-inch cut from the lightest cordless full-width mower ranked here.
products.description:
The EGO LM2114 is the only mower here with a full 21-inch deck, and it runs on EGO's 56V battery platform with the battery and charger included. It is a push-drive design, so there is no self-propel motor adding weight.

It ranks first because it fixes the usual trade-off: narrow light mowers mean more passes, and wide mowers are heavy. Against the Greenworks 40V below it, you get five more inches of deck and a larger battery platform, but you pay in the $200-500 bracket like the Greenworks and carry a bigger machine.

Buy it if you have a standard suburban lawn and want to finish in fewer passes. The caveat is that a 21-inch deck is overkill for a patio-sized yard, where a 14-inch model is easier to store.
products.idealFor: Standard-size lawns where you want fewer passes without a heavy self-propelled mower.
products.skipIf: Your yard is a small patio or garden strip that a 14-inch mower handles easily.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Mower with 4.0Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A sensible 16-inch cordless push mower for small to mid-size lawns.
products.description:
The Greenworks pairs a 16-inch deck with a 40V 4.0Ah battery, and the charger comes in the box. It is push drive only, which keeps the machine lighter than a self-propelled alternative.

It sits just below the EGO because the deck is five inches narrower, so a standard lawn takes more passes. In return it is easier to turn and store, and it still stays in the $200-500 bracket with a battery included.

Choose it for a small to mid-size lawn where you want cordless convenience without the bulk of a 21-inch mower. The caveat is that a 4.0Ah pack limits runtime on larger yards, so check your lawn size first.
products.idealFor: Small to mid-size lawns where you want cordless power without a heavy deck.
products.skipIf: You mow a large lawn and want the fewest possible passes.

products.name: Litheli Cordless Lawn Mower 14-Inch, Brushless Motor with 5.0Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: The cheapest way into a cordless brushless mower for a small yard.
products.description:
This Litheli has a 14-inch deck, a brushless motor and a 5.0Ah battery with charger, all in the $50-100 bracket. It also offers 5-position height adjustment, which is more than the simplest budget models provide.

It ranks below the Greenworks because the deck is two inches narrower and the brand is less established. It beats the corded mowers on convenience, since there is no cable to snag on flower beds.

Buy it for a yard under roughly 3,000 square feet where low cost and low weight matter most. The caveat is that the narrow deck makes larger lawns a slog.
products.idealFor: Small yards under about 3,000 square feet on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You have a standard-size lawn and want a wide deck.

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1114K Electric Corded Lawn Mower, 15-Inch, 11 Amp
products.verdict: An 11 amp corded push mower with more width than a reel mower.
products.description:
The LawnMaster uses an 11 amp corded motor behind a 15-inch deck and push drive. With no battery to buy or replace, the ongoing cost is the extension cord.

It lands fourth because the cord restricts where you can mow, which the cordless Litheli and Greenworks avoid. It gives you more width than the reel mower and more power than the smaller BLACK+DECKER, and sits in the $100-200 bracket.

Choose it for a small, open yard near an outlet. The caveat is the cable: trees, beds and corners make managing it tedious.
products.idealFor: Small open yards near an outlet.
products.skipIf: Your lawn has trees, beds or corners that would snag a cord.

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1204-14 14-Inch 4-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: No battery, no cord, no fuel: the lightest way to cut a small lawn.
products.description:
The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 is a manual reel mower with a 14-inch cutting width and four blades. It uses no battery, cord or fuel, so there is nothing to charge and nothing to carry beyond the frame.

It scores below the cordless models because you supply all the power, which suits flat lawns mowed often and punishes tall or thick grass. It undercuts every motorized pick on cost in the $50-100 bracket.

Buy it if true minimum weight and silence matter on a small, flat lawn. The caveat is that skipping a week of mowing makes this reel work much harder.
products.skipIf: You let the grass grow tall between cuts.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 3-in-1 Corded Lawn Mower, Weed Eater, and Edger (BESTA512CM)
products.verdict: A small 12-inch corded tool that doubles as a trimmer and edger.
products.description:
The BESTA512CM combines a mower, a weed eater and an edger in one 6.5 amp corded unit with a 12-inch cutting width. It is the smallest deck here and adds trimming duties that the others do not cover.

It ranks last because 12 inches and 6.5 amps make it a patch tool rather than a main mower. It does cost less than the LawnMaster in the $50-100 bracket, and it replaces two other tools.

Choose it for small patches, edges and patio-adjacent grass. The caveat is that it is not the right tool for a full lawn.
products.idealFor: Small patches and edging around a patio.
products.skipIf: You need a main mower for a whole lawn.

methodology.title: Lawn fit
methodology.description: Every pick is matched to the lawn size and type its spec sheet supports.

whatMatters.detail: Cutting width is the deck size in inches, and it sets how many passes a lawn needs. A 21-inch deck covers a stripe 50 percent wider than a 14-inch one. Check the number in the product title, not a marketing phrase.

Power source means manual reel, corded electric or battery. Corded mowers need an outlet and a cable, and battery mowers need charging. Look for the amp or volt figure in the title to tell which type you are buying.

Some cordless listings sell the bare tool only. A battery and charger can cost a large share of the total. Confirm the listing says 'battery and charger included' and note the Ah rating, since higher Ah means longer runtime.
Height adjustment sets how tall the grass stays after cutting. More positions let you adapt to season and lawn type. Look for a stated number of positions, like five, on the spec sheet.
Drive type is push or self-propelled. Self-propelled adds a motor and weight, while push keeps the machine light. Every pick here is push or manual, so check the listing if you want more assistance.

faq.q: Is a corded or cordless mower lighter?
faq.a: The spec sheets here do not list weights, so check each listing. Corded mowers carry no battery, but you drag a cable. A reel mower carries no motor at all.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with light mowers?
faq.a: They buy by weight alone and end up with a deck too narrow for their lawn. A 14-inch deck on a standard lawn means many extra passes.

faq.q: Is the EGO worth it over the Greenworks?
faq.a: If your lawn is standard size, the 21-inch deck saves real time. For a small lawn, the 16-inch Greenworks is easier to handle and stays in the same bracket.

faq.q: Does a reel mower need setup?
faq.a: The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 uses a manual 4-blade reel with no battery or fuel. Set your height, then push. Mow often so the grass stays short.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cordless mower?
faq.a: Store the battery indoors, charge it with the supplied charger and clear grass from the deck after use. Check the listing for each brand's care guidance.

faq.q: Can I use a corded mower on a large lawn?
faq.a: You can, but cable management becomes tedious. The LawnMaster is best for small, open yards near an outlet.

finalTake: For most people the EGO POWER+ 21-Inch is the best lightweight pick because it combines full width with cordless freedom. The Greenworks 40V 16-Inch suits smaller lawns, and the Litheli 14-Inch is the budget choice. Pick the American Lawn Mower reel only if your lawn is flat and you mow often.
